about: The closed set of names the watchdog may raise, and the component each one speaks about. Read by scripts/monitor.py (it puts the component beside every name it files, so a reader can tell a probe failure from a worker failure) and by tests/test_watchdog_issues.py (which fails when either emitter produces a name this file does not hold). A name is a claim about ONE component: on 2026-11-01 a probe reported its own failure under the worker's name across 173 records and paged for fourteen hours, which is the failure this registry exists to prevent.

host_clock_skew.meaning: this box's clock is further from a time authority than 30s. AnkiWeb refuses the sync and says 'your clock is not set to the correct time', which is the vendor's sentence and not the diagnosis.

api_unreachable.meaning: nothing answered on 127.0.0.1:8787/v1/health. The service is down or not listening, which is a fact about the API and not about the worker.

api_unhealthy.meaning: the API answered and said its status is not 'ok'. It is up and reporting itself unwell, which is a different repair from an API that is not there.

probe_cannot_run.meaning: the watchdog could not ask the worker anything at all: docker exec failed, or ops-check produced no parsable report. This is NEVER a statement about the worker - reporting it as one paged the operator for fourteen hours on 2026-11-01 while the worker was fine.

worker_probe_failed.meaning: the probe ran, exited non-zero, and named no issue of its own. The failure is the probe's own, which is why it is not spelled worker_probe_unavailable.

worker_heartbeat_missing.meaning: the worker has never written its heartbeat file. It is not running, or it has never started.

worker_heartbeat_stale.meaning: the heartbeat file exists and has not been touched for over fifteen minutes. The process is there or was, and has stopped working.

pending_jobs_overdue.meaning: at least one job has been pending past its next_attempt_at by more than fifteen minutes. Work is waiting and nothing is picking it up.

failed_jobs.meaning: at least one job is in the failed state. A capture did not get processed and somebody has to decide whether to retry it.

running_job_lease_expired.meaning: a job is marked running and its lease has expired or was never set. The worker that took it is gone, so the job is stuck rather than in progress.

application_alerts_unacknowledged.meaning: an open alert is still standing within its horizon. Past its horizon it expires on its own and is history, which is why this counts standing() and not every open row.

backup_missing_or_stale.meaning: there is no completed backup run, or the newest one is more than thirty hours old. Nothing is protecting the data.

scheduled_sync_overdue.meaning: a user with a local collection has no scheduler state, or its next sync is more than half an hour past. The Anki collection is drifting from what the learner expects.

database_probe_failed.meaning: the read-only queries against wortling.sqlite3 raised. The service's own store could not be read, so none of the queue, alert, backup or scheduler signals in this run mean anything.

provider_auth_or_availability_failed.meaning: the configured provider answered the /models probe with a non-2xx status. The token or the endpoint is wrong or the provider is down.

configured_models_unavailable.meaning: the provider answered and does not offer every model this deployment is configured to use. Calls will fail for the ones that are missing.

provider_probe_failed.meaning: the /models probe raised before it got a status. The exception class rides in metrics.provider_probe_error, because 'provider_probe_failed' alone sent a crew member into the container to find out what it was.
